rules.why: Sean, captain's log 002 (2026-10-20, Oliver's): "the wheels need to be few and far between ... they need to come in and hit when Brallin or when Shabraz are on the table ... those should be finisher kind of things where it's like Shabraz and Brallin are already out, they're kind of big, and I'm gonna drop a wheel on them." The model had been firing a wheel on any thin hand, which is early tempo — the play he says is wrong. Hold every wheel, spell or activated, until a commander is on the battlefield; the thin-hand clause then never fires on its own.

Sean, captain's log 002: "I don't even know if I should have held the hand that I had, because I only had one playable creature in it and a bunch of wheels." A keep has at most one wheel and at least one body or one ramp piece. Reported as a pass rate on the hand the model kept — the model still mulligans by its own 2-5-land rule, so every other figure stays comparable.

Sean, 2026-11-06, turning Sharknado Shabraz-first: "Brallin only comes in to give sharks trample at the end (and to give us access to lovely red cards!!!)" and "Brallin is not intended to come out early". The model had cast Brallin on his own curve, around turn 3.7, ahead of Shabraz at 4.8, so four mana went into the partner before the shark every game. Hold the partner until Shabraz is on the battlefield, then cast him last in the main phase, from what the turn left.
